title: Title and Gospel text of the homily
english: In the statements made about both his divinity and his humanity, he places the “I,” so that the meaning of the words is shown by their context, while the distinction of the natures is shown by the difference in what is said. And because he speaks in both cases as of one person, he signifies the union of the person.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Homilia in illud Ego vado ad patrem meum u01-rem-early
orientation: This is the opening title of Cyril of Jerusalem's homily, giving the Gospel saying on which he will preach.

title: The I placed on both natures
english: Christ uses the pronoun “I” for statements about both his divinity and his humanity, so that the meaning of the words is shown by their context, while the distinction of the natures is shown by the difference in what is said.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Homilia in illud Ego vado ad patrem meum u01-rem-mid
orientation: Cyril is explaining how the pronoun “I” in Christ’s saying is used of both his divinity and his humanity.

title: The union of the person shown by speaking as of one
english: The distinction of the natures is known from the difference in what is said; but by speaking in both cases as of one person, he signifies the union of the person.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Homilia in illud Ego vado ad patrem meum u01-rem-close
orientation: Cyril is concluding his explanation of how Christ's saying uses the pronoun “I” of both natures.
